nodes.label: README project overview
nodes.description: Best City Spots is presented as a premium high-fidelity urban intelligence platform with Liquid Glass UI, AI insights, city search, weather, analytics, Supabase caching, and Docker-ready deployment.

nodes.label: Liquid Glass design system
nodes.description: A visual system based on deep blacks, high-saturation blurs, refraction effects, atmospheric motion, technical typography, and dark/light theming.

nodes.label: AI city intelligence
nodes.description: Gemini-generated city briefings and travel trends validated with Zod and cached in Supabase for low latency and cost control.

nodes.label: Google Places Bayesian ranking
nodes.description: Experiences, dining, and stays are fetched from Google Places API New and ranked with a Bayesian ranking engine, including BlurHash image placeholders.

nodes.label: Weather and AQI fusion
nodes.description: Live conditions are sourced from OpenWeatherMap and PM2.5 air-quality inputs from Open-Meteo with a 60-minute cache.

nodes.label: multi-mode city search
nodes.description: Search combines Postgres FTS, fuzzy matching, aliases, GPS nearest-city lookup, and localStorage-persisted recent searches.

nodes.label: layered Supabase TTL caching
nodes.description: The app uses Supabase caches with long AI TTLs, medium places TTLs with soft refresh, 24-hour trending data, and 60-minute weather data to reduce provider cost and improve speed.

nodes.label: privacy-first visitor analytics
nodes.description: Analytics stores aggregate daily tables for visitor counts, traffic sources, devices, geography with geo consent, city views, and user actions without per-user profiles.

nodes.label: Zod, RLS, and hardened headers baseline
nodes.description: The security posture combines strict Zod input validation, Supabase Row Level Security, eslint-plugin-security, and hardened response headers in next.config.ts.
nodes.norm_label: zod, rls, and hardened headers baseline

nodes.label: Next.js 16 App Router stack
nodes.description: The application stack includes Next.js 16 App Router, React 19, TypeScript 5 strict mode, Tailwind CSS 4, Supabase, Framer Motion, next-themes, Lucide React, Sharp, BlurHash, ESLint 9, and npm.

nodes.label: layered monolith architecture
nodes.description: AGENTS.md defines Best City Spots as one Next.js app whose backend lives in route handlers, server actions, and server-only service modules rather than GraphQL, microservices, or event streaming.

nodes.label: thin routes with src/lib business logic
nodes.description: Route handlers and server actions should parse, validate, and shape responses, while provider calls, cache orchestration, Supabase access, and business rules live under src/lib.
nodes.norm_label: thin routes with src/lib business logic

nodes.label: Postgres RPC for heavy data behavior
nodes.description: Search, analytics aggregation, and atomic write behaviors should remain in Supabase SQL/RPC functions where database locality and concurrency matter.
nodes.norm_label: postgres rpc for heavy data behavior

nodes.label: public-read and service-role write boundary
nodes.description: The app is mostly public-read, but sensitive writes use server-only service role credentials; SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY must never reach client bundles.

nodes.label: graceful degradation for read paths
nodes.description: User-facing reads should return null, empty arrays, stale cache, or provider fallback where appropriate instead of failing hard on upstream issues.

nodes.label: lint type-check and targeted verification safety rails
nodes.description: Backend changes should use npm run lint, npm run type-check, and focused scripts or tests around ranking, validation, search, cache freshness, and analytics aggregation.
nodes.norm_label: lint type-check and targeted verification safety rails

nodes.label: strict TypeScript style
nodes.description: CODE_STYLE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md require strict TypeScript, explicit function signatures, no any, const for immutable values, typed props, and interfaces or types for structured data.

nodes.label: React functional component conventions
nodes.description: Components should be functional, typed, hook-order disciplined, accessible, stable-keyed, and avoid avoidable inline handlers or missing effect dependencies.

nodes.label: Tailwind accessibility and security style
nodes.description: Use Tailwind utilities rather than inline styles, semantic HTML and ARIA labels, input validation, environment variables for secrets, XSS prevention, and parameterized query patterns.

nodes.label: frontend performance coding guidelines
nodes.description: Memoize expensive work, debounce frequent input/API calls, code split large components, and use Next.js Image instead of raw img tags.

nodes.label: Conventional Commits and PR checklist
nodes.description: Contributions use Conventional Commit messages, atomic commits, self-review, documentation updates, lint/format/test checks, mobile and desktop verification, and clear PR descriptions.

nodes.label: Docker Compose web service
nodes.description: docker-compose.yml builds the web image from Dockerfile with public Supabase and Google API build args, exposes port 3000, sets HOSTNAME and PORT, injects SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY at runtime, loads .env.production, and restarts unless stopped.

nodes.label: graphify repository rules
nodes.description: CLAUDE.md says architecture/codebase questions should consult graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md or wiki output, and code modifications should rebuild the graph with graphify.watch.

nodes.label: award-winning travel website design 2026
nodes.description: The design research document defines world-class travel platforms as intent-aware, multimodal, adaptive, emotionally resonant, high-performing, accessible digital companions.

nodes.label: Designing for Intent
nodes.description: Interfaces should adapt to informational, navigational, commercial, and transactional intent, emphasizing relevant content and suppressing peripheral distraction.

nodes.label: multimodal experience design
nodes.description: Travel platforms should preserve state and context across voice, vision, touch, haptics, wearables, and screen-based interactions.

nodes.label: biophilic and organic UI
nodes.description: Natural textures, earth tones, asymmetrical flowing layouts, and hyperlocal visual motifs help travel interfaces feel grounded, calming, and culturally authentic.

nodes.label: fluid grids and container queries
nodes.description: The recommended responsive foundation uses relative units, CSS Grid auto-fit/minmax, Flexbox, intrinsic sizing, clamp(), and container queries for component-level adaptability.

nodes.label: typography of trust
nodes.description: Sophisticated travel typography pairs refined serif headings with readable sans-serif body text, using hierarchy and fluid type to convey authority and calm.

nodes.label: agentic personalized UI
nodes.description: World-class travel platforms behave as intelligent companions that adjust content and calls to action using context, time of day, persona, visit status, and natural-language goals.

nodes.label: hyperlocal storytelling
nodes.description: Authenticity is built with local culture, community-sourced imagery, local materials and crafts, transparent budgets, honest reviews, and customer-centered language.

nodes.label: front-end live audit findings
nodes.description: front-end_AUDIT.md validates current critical/high frontend issues around notes persistence, Unicode search, missing mobile navigation, skip-link accessibility, blocking home data, abort semantics, analytics reliability/privacy, and scroll progress ARIA.

nodes.label: note-key idempotency bug
nodes.description: experience-helpers can re-sanitize already sanitized note keys into k_k_ keys, causing saved notes to miss on reload or during draft/persist transitions.

nodes.label: Unicode city search input bug
nodes.description: CitySearch strips non-ASCII characters, blocking global city names such as Koln, Sao Paulo, Lodz, and Montreal variants with diacritics.

nodes.label: unmounted mobile bottom navigation
nodes.description: MobileBottomNav exists but is not mounted, while SiteFooter reserves mobile spacer height for a navigation element users never see.

nodes.label: skip-link and scroll progress accessibility regressions
nodes.description: The audit flags an invisible skip link pattern and a ScrollProgress component whose aria-valuenow remains static at 0 with an empty percentage label.
nodes.norm_label: skip-link and scroll progress accessibility regressions

nodes.label: abort timeout and analytics delivery risks
nodes.description: The audit flags httpFetch timeout bypass via caller signals, Promise.race without aborting places work, analytics fire-and-forget writes that may be dropped, string sendBeacon payloads, and full referrer capture.
nodes.norm_label: abort timeout and analytics delivery risks

nodes.label: front-end quick wins
nodes.description: The highest-impact frontend fixes include note-key idempotency, Unicode search, navigation decision, abort propagation, analytics waitUntil and Blob payloads, skip-link repair, Suspense and unstable_cache for trending, and targeted dead CSS removal.

nodes.label: backend performance audit report
nodes.description: AUDIT_REPORT.md records a backend performance audit where all critical and high issues were shipped, 78 of 79 total findings were closed, and only intentional places fan-out remains deferred.

nodes.label: Phase 6 optimization candidates
nodes.description: Post-audit opportunities include optimizing elastic search SQL, marking RPCs parallel safe, explicit city columns, EXPLAIN ANALYZE probes, embedded PostgREST reads, generateStaticParams, sphere route cache control, and a cities_lite view.

nodes.label: Supabase migration conventions
nodes.description: New schema changes should use ordered timestamped files in supabase/migrations, be idempotent, be small and one-concern, and avoid destructive changes mixed with additive changes.

nodes.label: fallback maintenance page
nodes.description: fallbackPage/index.html is a standalone noindex maintenance page with a dark glass card, animated gradient orbs, countdown timer persisted in localStorage, progress animation, support link, and auto-reload when the timer expires.

nodes.label: Google site verification file
nodes.description: public/google83792ae278071723.html contains the google-site-verification token for search console ownership verification.

nodes.description: data/city_ai_candidates.txt lists 1,000 candidate cities as city, country, and population records, ordered from megacities through smaller/null-population administrative places.

nodes.label: global city coverage with diacritics and null populations
nodes.description: The candidate data includes global names with diacritics and alternate political/geographic labels, plus null population values for some smaller administrative places.
